country.comment: Empirical study set in Ahmedabad, India, examining the Ahmedabad Slum Networking Project (SNP).
country.where_found: PDF p. 7, section 'The Context: Slum Upgrading in Ahmedabad, India'; PDF p. 8, 'Survey Design and Sampling Frame'

effect_estimate.comment: All primary quantitative estimates are reported as odds ratios and standard errors from four cross-sectional logistic regression models (Table 6).
effect_estimate.value: Among 300 surveyed CBO leaders/members in upgraded slums, 74.9% rated overall SNP quality 'very satisfactory', while 20.7% complained about poor water quality/quantity and 11.7% complained about poor sewerage quality/quantity. In multivariable logistic regressions, CBO meeting attendance increased odds of rating overall SNP quality 'very satisfactory' (OR = 2.27, SE = 0.08, p < 0.001; N = 298) but was not significantly associated with water complaints (OR = 1.44, SE = 0.28; N = 277). Instead, lower odds of complaining about water were associated with CBO frequency of approaching the municipality (OR = 0.60, SE = 0.14, p < 0.05), CBO frequency of approaching the sponsoring NGO (OR = 0.56, SE = 0.13, p < 0.05), CBO-NGO evaluation partnership (OR = 0.15, SE = 0.11, p < 0.05), and relative area wealth (OR = 0.07, SE = 0.06, p < 0.01), whereas distance in miles from central municipal offices increased water complaints (OR = 1.44, SE = 0.21, p < 0.05). For sewerage complaints (N = 300), CBO frequency of approaching the sponsoring NGO (OR = 0.50, SE = 0.13, p < 0.01) and regional project density (OR = 0.82, SE = 0.05, p < 0.001) reduced complaint odds, Gujarati primary language increased complaint odds (OR = 4.89, SE = 2.73, p < 0.01), and municipal contact was not statistically significant (OR = 1.56, SE = 0.42).
effect_estimate.where_found: PDF p. 9, 'Measuring Project Satisfaction'; Table 4, PDF p. 11; PDF pp. 11–15; Table 6, PDF p. 13

mechanism_certainty.comment: Capped at <= 2 by cross-sectional observational design; rated 1 (documented statistical association) because the study estimates cross-sectional correlations between self-reported CBO participation, NGO partnership, and municipal/NGO contact and respondent complaints/satisfaction regarding water and sewerage, while explicitly noting that perceived satisfaction/complaints only partially reflect actual physical service quality and inferring rather than directly observing how redress requests alter municipal service delivery.
mechanism_certainty.where_found: PDF pp. 10–15, 'Measuring Project Satisfaction' and 'Analysis: Relating Sustained Participation to Project Satisfaction'; Table 6, PDF p. 13; PDF pp. 16–17, 'Conclusion'

mechanism_flags.comment: Examines sustained community participation in CBOs (participation), approaching the municipality or sponsoring NGO to seek service redress as well as voicing negative service complaints (complaint / ENFORCEMENT), and intermediary NGO partnership/assistance helping CBOs navigate municipal service maintenance (bureaucratic_assistance / DISCRETION_ACCOMMODATION).
mechanism_flags.where_found: PDF pp. 7–8, 'The Context: Slum Upgrading in Ahmedabad, India'; PDF pp. 11–15; Table 5, PDF p. 12; Table 6, PDF p. 13

outcome_flags.comment: All sampled communities received household water supply and underground sewerage under the SNP, and the empirical outcomes model respondent complaints regarding poor quality or quantity of water and sewerage services.
outcome_flags.where_found: Table 1, PDF p. 7; PDF p. 11, 'Analysis: Relating Sustained Participation to Project Satisfaction'; Table 4, PDF p. 11; Table 6, PDF p. 13

risk_of_bias_tool.comment: Observational cross-sectional survey of participants within SNP-upgraded communities without a non-upgraded or quasi-experimental policy comparator; all reported estimates are cross-sectional multivariable logistic regressions (the brief, unreported 2SLS robustness check for covariate endogeneity does not establish a quasi-experimental intervention evaluation suitable for ROBINS-I).
risk_of_bias_tool.value: JBI Critical Appraisal Checklist for Analytical Cross Sectional Studies
risk_of_bias_tool.where_found: PDF p. 8, 'Survey Design and Sampling Frame'; PDF p. 11, 'Analysis: Relating Sustained Participation to Project Satisfaction'; Table 6, PDF p. 13

sample_size.comment: 320 individuals were randomly sampled via stratified sampling from ~500 leaders and members across 38 SNP-registered CBOs (out of 52 eligible CBOs from ~75 total); 300 completed surveys were analysed (cross-tabulation N = 299; logistic regression N = 298 for overall satisfaction, N = 277 for water complaints, N = 300 for sewerage complaints, and N = 300 for street lighting complaints).
sample_size.value: 300 CBO leaders and members across 38 neighbourhood organisations (from 320 sampled; regression N = 277–300)
sample_size.where_found: PDF p. 8, 'Survey Design and Sampling Frame'; Table 3, PDF p. 10; Table 4, PDF p. 11; Table 6, PDF p. 13

study_design.comment: Single-wave cross-sectional survey conducted January–June 2009 among leaders and members of SNP-upgraded CBOs, analysed using descriptive cross-tabulations and multivariable logistic regression models; the authors also mention running 2SLS instrumental-variable models to check for reverse causation/endogeneity with similar results, though no instruments or 2SLS estimates are reported.
study_design.value: Cross-sectional stratified random survey with multivariable logistic regression (and unreported 2SLS instrumental-variable sensitivity check)
study_design.where_found: PDF p. 2, Abstract; PDF p. 8, 'Survey Design and Sampling Frame'; PDF p. 11, 'Analysis: Relating Sustained Participation to Project Satisfaction'; Table 6, PDF p. 13

evidence_quotes.page: PDF p. 11, Analysis: Relating Sustained Participation to Project Satisfaction
evidence_quotes.quote: The four dependent variables selected as measures of satisfaction include whether the respondent reports being ‘very satisfied’ with overall project quality (‘‘snp_qual2’’), and whether the respondent complains about quantity or quality of water, sewerage and street lighting services.
Of the four variables included in this model, only attend is statistically significant.

evidence_quotes.page: PDF p. 14, Respondents' Complaints over Water Services
evidence_quotes.quote: These results suggest that respondents who are members of CBOs with a close partnering relationship with their sponsoring NGO, and/or have the ability to communicate their needs to either that NGO or to the municipality, are less likely to have complained about the quality or quantity of their water services.

evidence_quotes.page: PDF p. 15, Respondents' Complaints over Sewerage Services
evidence_quotes.quote: As in the water services model, respondents who report that their CBO has frequently contacted their sponsoring NGO to request service assistance (ngo_com) are less likely to make negative comments about their sewerage services than respondents who do not report that their CBO is in frequent contact with the sponsoring NGO.
